correctness.rationale: In basis 1,z^n/sqrt(n), positive-index Dirichlet matrix entries are sqrt(i/j)b_epsilon(i+j), while the zero row and column are o(1) after multiplying by epsilon in Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Beta/gamma bounds yield finite Hilbert-Schmidt sums for epsilon>0. Embed the positive indices in L²(0,infty) with intervals [epsilon log i, epsilon log(i+1)) to obtain step kernels epsilon sqrt(i/j)b_epsilon(i+j)/sqrt(ell_i ell_j). For a.e. x>y>0 they converge to e^(-x); for x<y to zero. The common C exp(-max(x,y)) square-integrable envelope proves HS convergence, hence norm/singular convergence, to Tf(x)=e^(-x)int_0^x f(y)dy. T*T kernel is e^(-2max(y,z))/2; differentiating its eigen-equation yields lambda(f_double_prime+2f_prime)+e^(-2y)f=0 and f_prime(0)=0, whose square-integrable solution e^(-y)J_1(e^(-y)/sqrt(lambda)) requires J_0(1/sqrt(lambda))=0. HS trace integral int_0^infty xe^(-2x)dx=1/4. At epsilon=0, input 1 produces divergent sum_i i/(i+1)^2. The packaged check.py was examined but its 54 recorded finite checks are not proof of this operator limit.
residual_risks: The singular-value law is fixed-k only, not uniform in k; beta moments unnormalized and D norm fixed as displayed.
Uniform beta/gamma asymptotics and Sturm–Liouville solution invoke standard established analytic identities.
